To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the new measure of control beliefs in three domains yielded a factor structure that clearly supported separation of cognitive, social, health domains; showed generally low correlations among the factors; showed satisfactory reliabilities of the factors, and showed that control beliefs in the cognitive domain were stable across the adult life span, but that there was a significant decline in perceived control in the health domain for individuals in their 70's and a significant decline in the social domain for individuals in the 40's, 50's, and
the three factors of control beliefs are clearly separable in terms of content and that control beliefs are relatively stable across age until the 7th decade.

the new measure of perceived domain specific control yields three clearly distinguishable factors, and that age-related differences in the cognitive, the health, and the social domain of control beliefs were found.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new instrument for assessing perceived control.
the question whether the perception of control in specific domains changes with age.
the development of a measure of perceived control that is sensitive to age differences and to the specific domain of perceived control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
control beliefs in specific age groups are domain specific, and that control beliefs in the health domain are generally more stable across the life span than control beliefs in the other domains.
control beliefs in the various domains are stable across adulthood until the 70th year of life.
the new assessment of control beliefs appears to be a valid measure of perceived control in the cognitive and social domains and a promising measure in the health domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new measure is a promising instrument for the assessment of perceived self-control, which can be applied to various life domains.
the measure of control beliefs in specific life domains appears to be a useful tool for the study of perceived control and aging.
this measure is a promising new tool to assess the construct of perceived control in specific domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
control beliefs can be measured in three domains with a new instrument that yields satisfactory psychometric properties.
perceived control is not a unitary construct, and that it is important to assess control beliefs separately for different domains of life.
the new measure of perceived domain-specific control beliefs has good reliability and is a promising instrument for further research in the field of aging.
